newsitem.title: USA: Plains cattle markets quiet, few $70 bids - private.
newsitem.headline: Plains cattle markets quiet, few $70 bids - private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet early Tuesday, with a few feedlots passing $70.00 per cwt bids, feedlot sources said.
Some sources said more packers were bidding $70.00 Tuesday, compared with Monday when only a few $70.00 bids were reported as well as some at $71.00.
The $70.00 bids are $2.00 lower than trades late last week at $72.00.
Feedlot sources said cattle were priced at $73.00, but they said bids of $72.00 would result in trading.
Feedlots continue to ship cattle sold last week. Some feedyards have shipped all of last week's sales, while others said cattle sold late in the week remain in the pens.
"We shipped quite a bit of cattle this morning," said a Kansas feedlot manager.
